items.title: Deepseek V4.1 Flash 1017 beats larger rivals in agentic tasks while once again massively cutting per-task costs
items.summary: Deepseek has released V4.1-Flash-1017 as an open-weight model that posts better benchmarks, finishes tasks faster, and produces shorter outputs than its predecessor. The company is also opening up its internal search engine through new Search and Fetch APIs at $0.75 per 1,000 calls. API users in tools like Claude Code and Codex get free access for now....

items.title: Replit makes OpenAI its default over Anthropic, CEO says
items.summary: Over the weekend, Masad clarified that OpenAI would replace Anthropic as its default model provider. Claude will still be available to customers on the platform.

items.title: AI agents have bad taste in long-term decisions and a new benchmark proves it
items.summary: A new benchmark called Taste-Bench tests how well AI agents make strategic choices during long-running tasks. Even the best model, GPT-5.6 Sol, picks the right path on just under 60 percent of simple binary questions. Thinking longer doesn't help. The article AI agents have bad taste in long-term decisions and a new benchmark proves it appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: An OpenAI model hacked a government site, grabbed 24 years of hospital data and kept it quiet
items.summary: OpenAI has published four new cases where its AI models bypassed security boundaries on their own during training or testing. In one case, a model extracted server passwords from a government website, forged authorization tokens, and downloaded 24 years of hospital data without mentioning the unauthorized access....

items.title: AI models hide mistakes in their own work reports, but one sentence in your prompt can help
items.summary: AI agents systematically skip errors in their own reports, even when they spot the problems. In a study by Google Research, MIT, and Harvard, GPT-5.5 left out negative results in 198 out of 200 paper abstracts. The article AI models hide mistakes in their own work reports, but one sentence in your prompt can help appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
items.summary: According to Elorian's evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.

items.title: AI in Production: Panellists Highlight Silent Failures, Harness Engineering, and Agent Governance
items.summary: A recent InfoQ webinar examined operational challenges in deploying agentic systems. Key points included issues like semantic and embedding drift, which can lead to significant errors. Experts discussed the need for automated code reviews, continuous evaluation of models, and enhanced privacy measures. The session emphasised a strategic approach to deployment and security management. By Olimpiu Pop

items.title: Anthropic proposes AI safety bill with $1B / 50-death treshold
items.summary: Tin AI từ Hacker News AI về "Anthropic proposes AI safety bill with $1B / 50-death treshold". Mở bài gốc để đọc chi tiết và đánh giá tác động với team.

items.title: Reverse Engineer Anything Project Brings AI Agents to Binary Analysis
items.summary: Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) is an open-source project with over 200K GitHub stars that connects coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex to reverse-engineering tools like Ghidra, Hopper, and IDA. The project lets developers inspect compiled binaries, trace function calls, and investigate how applications implement specific features. By Renato Losio

items.title: AWS Introduces Strands Decider 2B and Strands Box for AI Agent Development
items.summary: AWS has introduced two open-source projects for AI agent development: Strands Decider 2B, a small model designed to make decisions within agent workflows, and Strands Box, a sandbox for controlling agent execution. Both projects address different aspects of building agents that use tools, execute code, and interact with external systems. By Daniel Dominguez
